title: Weak versus Public Indifferentiability
summary: Public indifferentiability implies its weak variant; whether the converse holds for every scheme or the notions can be separated remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether, for every scheme $\Pi$, $\Pi$ satisfying weak public indifferentiability implies that $\Pi$ satisfies public indifferentiability. Either prove this implication or construct a scheme $\Pi$ that satisfies weak public indifferentiability but not public indifferentiability. The implication appears difficult to prove, and no such separating scheme is currently known.

scope.domain: Structural comparison of public and weak public indifferentiability for cryptographic schemes.
parameters: Π: an arbitrary scheme whose two indifferentiability properties are compared
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that weak public indifferentiability implies public indifferentiability for every scheme, or construct a scheme separating the two notions.

citations.label: A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs

progress.summary: The paper establishes the implication from public to weak public indifferentiability, then notes that the reverse appears difficult to prove and that no separating example is known.
citation_labels: Akinori Hosoyamada et al., A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs
